 After all of the Halloween excitement, it's time to prepare for a new month. 
 In case you haven't changed your clocks yet, daylight saving time has come to an end, which means we've gained an hour overnight (perfect after a Halloween night or Sunday snooze!) 
 7-DAY FORECAST | INTERACTIVE RADAR 
 While October rain was lacking compared to average, hopefully November can help us catch up. 
 For now, skies remain dry with typical fall weather. Daytime highs stay in the mid to upper-50s through Friday, with overnight lows between the low to mid-40s. 
 Many mornings will start with patchy fog, followed by clouds. Today, those clouds will eventually turn to sunshine towards the afternoon. 
 Our next chance for rain could arrive as early as Wednesday night. There's still some uncertainty as to what that would look like, but those rain chances last through Friday. 
 For now, enjoy the sweater weather! 
 SUNDAY (Nov. 1) - Dense Fog Advisory until 10 a.m. Patchy fog and frost in the morning. Mostly cloudy skies, gradually becoming sunny. High 55/Low 41. 
 MONDAY (Nov. 2) - Morning patchy fog, then cloudy. High 57/Low 39. 
 TUESDAY (Nov. 3) - Cloudy morning, then partly sunny. High 60/Low 46. 
 WEDNESDAY (Nov. 4) - Partly sunny. Patchy fog. Rain likely in the afternoon. High 58/Low 42. 
 THURSDAY (Nov. 5) - Partly sunny, slight chance of rain (20%). High 59/Low 47. 
 FRIDAY(Nov. 6) - Rain likely (60%). Mostly cloudy. High 57/Low 45.
